title: Κάμηλος τὸ πρῶτον ὀφθείς
titleEn: The Camel Seen for the First Time
part: The Camel Seen for the First Time (Chambry 148 · Perry 195)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 148 (= Perry 195). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὅτε πρῶτον κάμηλος ὤφθη, οἱ ἄνθρωποι φοβηθέντες καὶ τὸ μέγεθος καταπλαγέντες ἔφευγον.
sentences.tr: Hote prōton kamēlos ōphthē, hoi anthrōpoi phobēthentes kai to megethos kataplagentes epheugon.
sentences.l: When first a camel was seen, men, having taken fright and been struck with amazement at her size, kept fleeing.
sentences.i: When a camel was first seen, men took fright, and astounded at her size, ran away.
sentences.n: ὤφθη is the aorist passive of ὁράω. καταπλήσσω, "strike down", is used in the passive of the blow amazement deals; τὸ μέγεθος is an accusative of respect — struck with amazement in respect of her size. The imperfect ἔφευγον gives the flight as something that went on and on, not a single act.

sentences.t: Ὡς δέ, χρόνου προϊόντος, συνεῖδον αὐτῆς τὸ πρᾷον, ἐθάρρησαν μέχρι τοῦ προσελθεῖν.
sentences.tr: Hōs de, chronou proiontos, syneidon autēs to prāion, etharrēsan mechri tou proselthein.
sentences.l: But when, time going forward, they perceived her gentleness, they took courage as far as approaching.
sentences.i: But as time went on and they saw how gentle she was, they grew bold enough to come near.
sentences.n: χρόνου προϊόντος is a genitive absolute. τὸ πρᾷον is the neuter adjective standing as a noun, "the gentle thing about her". μέχρι τοῦ προσελθεῖν is an articular infinitive under a preposition, the regular way of naming how far something went.

sentences.t: Αἰσθόμενοι δὲ κατὰ μικρὸν ὡς χολὴν τὸ ζῷον οὐκ ἔχει, εἰς τοῦτο καταφρονήσεως ἦλθον ὥστε καὶ χαλινὸν αὐτῇ περιθέντες παισὶν ἐλαύνειν αὐτὴν ἔδωκαν.
sentences.tr: Aisthomenoi de kata mikron hōs cholēn to zōion ouk echei, eis touto kataphronēseōs ēlthon hōste kai chalinon autēi perithentes paisin elaunein autēn edōkan.
sentences.l: And perceiving little by little that the animal has no gall, they came to such a point of contempt that, having put a bridle round her, they even gave her to boys to drive.
sentences.i: And perceiving by degrees that the beast has no gall in it, they came to such contempt that they put a bridle on her and handed her over to boys to drive.
sentences.n: χολή, gall, is the seat of anger in Greek physiology, so a creature with no gall has no temper to fear. εἰς τοῦτο καταφρονήσεως, "to this point of contempt", takes the genitive of the thing measured and looks forward to the ὥστε clause; ὥστε with the indicative ἔδωκαν states the result as something that actually happened.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι τὰ φοβερὰ τῶν πραγμάτων ἡ συνήθεια καταπραΰνει.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti ta phobera tōn pragmatōn hē synētheia katapraynei.
sentences.l: The story shows that familiarity makes gentle the fearful among things.
sentences.i: The story shows that familiarity takes the terror out of frightening things.
sentences.n: τὰ φοβερὰ τῶν πραγμάτων is a partitive genitive under a neuter adjective, "the frightening ones among things". συνήθεια is being used to a thing. Chambry prints καταπραΰνει here with the diaeresis, marking the υ as a syllable of its own (πραΰς, "gentle"); the same moral at fable 42 is printed without it.
